correctness.rationale: For every n>=2 and alpha>=0 with s<1, P=(t I+alpha 1^T)Q with t=1-s and Q column stochastic. The first factor has determinant t^(n-1) and adjugate t^(n-2)(I-alpha 1^T); the adjugate norm is separately convex in the stochastic columns, so a deterministic map attains its maximum. The only nonzero deterministic cases are permutations with norm t^(n-2)(1+s-2 min alpha) and rank-(n-1) maps with norm 2t^(n-2)max(1-alpha_k,alpha_k). Their maximum is exactly 2(1-min alpha)t^(n-2). A perturbation adding probability delta to the missing output yields invertible P_delta and the same limiting determinant-weighted inverse norm. The packaged standard-library checker passed 1253 direct rational-minor assertions; finite checks are supplementary.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new result has an exact optimizing class at rank n-1. Goldberg determinant equality instead requires an invertible permutation-type residual, and the sharp determinant value cannot be inserted into the inverse norm without a separate inverse estimate. The 2026 universal asymptotic is insufficient to recover either its absolute constant or its minorant parameter dependence. No tested primary statement therefore implies the theorem as a corollary.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: For invertible P, the functional equals |det P| ||P^{-1}||_1, not |det P| alone; the maximizing stochastic limit in the new theorem is rank n-1, hence its determinant is zero while the adjugate norm is maximal. This rules out identifying the target with the existing determinant-only problem. Neither the universal asymptotic Schäffer constant nor an inverse-group-resolvent estimate is equivalent to this sharp fixed-minorant finite-order supremum.

value.rationale: A fixed nonuniform Doeblin vector is an intrinsic property of a finite Markov operator, and the adjugate norm is the natural determinant-weighted inverse stability functional. The theorem supplies the exact dimension- and minorant-dependent extremum with explicit rank-deficient extremizers and invertible approximations. The sharp uniform refresh profile 2(1-theta/n)(1-theta)^(n-2) shows exponential suppression absent for unmixed Markov operators. Its value is a natural all-orders sharp endpoint stability problem, not an arbitrary computed slice.
